chunks: Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥarth ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily Allah loves the one who admits [his sins] and repents often. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to turn to Allah in repentance seventy times a day without having committed any sin. I asked: Would he say: I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn back to Him in repentance? He replied: He would say: I turn [penitently] to Allah.

key_terms.أَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ: I turn to Allah in repentance

ai.seo_question: How often did the Prophet Muhammad repent to Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawbah* as a continuous state of spiritual refinement rather than merely a response to sin, exemplified by the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) practice of repenting seventy times daily. The Imam clarifies that this frequent utterance of 'I repent to Allah' reflects profound humility and constant awareness of divine presence, reinforcing the concept that even the infallible engage in self-accountability to elevate their spiritual station.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 11.Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥarth ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said, “Verily Allah loves the one who admits [his sins] and repents often.”

He [then] said, “The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) used to turn to Allah in repentance seventy times a day without having committed any sin.” The narrator asked, “Would he say: I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn back to Him in repentance?” He (a) replied, “He would say: I turn [penitently] to Allah.”
